preamble: Depalatalization of the voiced alveolo-palatal fricative [ʑ] to the plain alveolar fricative [z]. It is part of Kashubian 'kaszëbienié' (Kashubization): the Proto-Slavic soft dentals t, d, s, z before front vowels first became alveolo-palatal [tɕ dʑ ɕ ʑ], as they still are in Polish, and then in Kashubian lost their palatality to [ts dz s z]. Kashubian therefore has z where Polish has ź/zi: zëma /ˈzɜ.ma/ against Polish zima /ˈʑi.ma/, zemia /ˈzɛ.mja/ against ziemia, zôrno /ˈzɞr.nɔ/ against ziarno. After the hardened consonant short i shifted to ë, as in zëma.
